details.publicNotes:
Hatemongers stoke up hatred, prejudice, and paranoia with relish and fervor. Though they enjoy being the center of attention and holding power over others, most hatemongers would rather be a trusted advisor or an influential demagogue than a ruler. They believe that establishing complete control over a community stifles people's ability to invent their own methods of cruelty and oppression.

A hatemonger might even work to oust a more obviously malevolent controlling force from a community to make room for their own schemes, earning acclaim and respect in the process. Though they are capable combatants, hatemongers rarely deal a lethal blow to an enemy, preferring to entice others to experience ending a life.

Mundane Origins

Many have speculated that a hatemonger in their true form must be demonic or diabolic in appearance. Sadly, this is not the case. Though their powers are supernatural, their existence isn't: hatemongers can arise from any mortal ancestry and seem to do so spontaneously, without any outside influence. Some idealistic philosophers hold the belief that the eradication and destruction of the last hatemongers will lead to their extinction as a species. More likely, only by eradicating hatred itself will prevent new hatemongers from being created—an even more unrealistic proposition than defeating the hatemongers themselves.

A vision of apocalyptic destruction fills the mind of each creature in the area. The vision deals 11d6 mental damage (basic Will save). On a critical failure, the creature must also succeed at a Reflex save or believe it's trapped (stuck in a fissure, adrift at sea, or some other fate in keeping with its vision). If it fails the second save, it's also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned} for 1 minute. It can attempt a new Will save at the end of each of its turns, and on a success, it disbelieves the illusion and recovers from the Stunned condition.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

Your honeyed words are difficult for creatures to resist. You suggest a course of action to the target, which must be phrased in such a way as to seem like a logical course of action to the target and can't be self-destructive or obviously against the target's self-interest. The target must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and knows you tried to control it.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The target immediately follows your suggestion. The spell has a duration of 1 minute, or until the target has completed a finite suggestion or the suggestion becomes self-destructive or has other obvious negative effects.

Critical Failure As failure, but the base duration is 1 hour.

Heightened (8th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

Illusory pain wracks the target, dealing 2d4 mental damage and @Damage[(@item.level)d4[persistent,mental]] damage. The target must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes full initial damage but no persistent damage, and the spell ends immediately.

Failure The target takes full initial and persistent damage, and the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}. If the target recovers from being Sickened, the persistent damage ends and the spell ends.

Critical Failure As failure, but the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d4 and the persistent damage by 1d4.

You bypass your targets' rational minds, instilling them with unshakable conviction and zeal. The targets each gain 12 temporary Hit Points and a +2 status bonus to Will saves against mental effects, as their faith overrides the signals from their own bodies and minds. If you tell a target to do something, it must comply with your request, though if it would normally find the task repugnant, it can attempt a Will save at the end of its turn each round due to the cognitive dissonance. On a success, it ends the spell's effects on itself entirely.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.nemThuhp3praALY6]{Spell Effect: Zealous Conviction}

Heightened (9th) The temporary Hit Points increase to 18, and the status bonus to Will saves increases to +3.

You cast your thoughts through a creature's mind, sifting for information. You access the target's memories and knowledge unless it fends you off with a Will save.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure Each round of the spell's duration, you can Sustain the spell to ask a different question and attempt to uncover the answer. For each question, the target can attempt a Deception check against your spell DC; if the target succeeds, you don't learn the answer, and on a critical success, the target gives you a false answer that you believe is truthful Once you've asked the target a given question, asking it again, even with a separate casting of mind probe, produces the same result.

Critical Failure As failure, and the target takes a –4 circumstance penalty to Deception checks against your questions.

You afflict the target with a curse that makes its presence abrasive and off-putting. The target must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success For 10 minutes, the target must roll twice and use the worse result whenever attempting a Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, or Performance check, and creatures they encounter have an initial attitude toward them of one step worse (for instance, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.I1ffBVISxLr2gC4u]{Unfriendly} instead of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fuG8dgthlDWfWjIA]{Indifferent}).

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.hlgCesYXXHG8r9X4]{Spell Effect: Outcast's Curse (Success)}

Failure As success, but the effect is permanent.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.QccOlLHtnVEmD67m]{Spell Effect: Outcast's Curse (Failure)}

Critical Failure As failure, and creatures that the target encounters have an initial attitude toward them of two steps worse.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

Trigger The hatemonger takes damage from a successful Strike or spell attack roll

Effect The hatemonger directs a follower to get revenge. They choose one ally of 13th level or lower within 30 feet. That ally either Strides toward or makes a Strike against the triggering creature. This Strike neither applies nor counts toward any creature's multiple attack penalty.

The hatemonger can take on the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage modifiers with their Strikes, but it might change the damage type their Strikes deal.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

Requirements At least two creatures within 30 feet are frightened

Effect The hatemonger feeds on fear. All frightened creatures within 30 feet take @Damage[7d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:33|basic] save). The hatemonger gains a number of temporary Hit Points equal to the highest damage a single creature takes from this effect, and then can't use Echo Chamber again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Echo Chamber]]{1d4 rounds}.

The hatemonger inspires fear, hatred, and violence. Each creature within 30 feet must attempt a @Check[will|dc:33] save. A creature that succeeds at the saving throw is temporarily immune to Stoke Hatred for 1 hour.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success For 1 round, the target gains a +2 status bonus on damage rolls and takes a –1 status penalty to AC. @UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.effects.Item.1ValspI2V8dmxibX]{Effect: Stoke Hatred (Success)}

Failure The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}. The target can't reduce their frightened condition at the end of their turn unless it used a hostile action in that turn. While they are frightened, they gain a +4 status bonus on damage rolls. @UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.effects.Item.mFLmqvo8cLcLvF1e]{Effect: Stoke Hatred (Failure)}

Critical Failure As failure, except the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for as long as it remains frightened.

After spending a minute talking to a willing creature, the hatemonger can amplify the creature's hatred. The target receives a +2 status bonus to Intimidation checks and damage rolls against people that they hate; this increases to a +4 status bonus against creatures that are frightened from an effect that they caused. However, whenever the target gains the frightened condition, the condition's value is 1 higher than normal. All attempts to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coerce} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie} to the target in an attempt to stoke hatred receive a result that is one degree of success higher than what was rolled. These effects last until the target makes a meaningful attempt to assist someone that they hate.
